title: Menemen
subtitle: Turkish tomato and pepper egg scramble
excerpt: Menemen is a loose, saucy Turkish scrambled egg dish cooked in a sofrito of peppers and tomatoes. Eggs go in at the very end and need only a minute off the heat to set into a silky, custardy mass. It is the Turkish answer to shakshuka, but the egg is stirred rather than poached.
sourceNotes: A household staple across Turkey, eaten from breakfast through to supper. The name refers to the town of Menemen in Izmir province.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The pepper and tomato base keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat gently and stir in fresh eggs to order.

content.text: Menemen is a Turkish breakfast that starts like ratatouille and ends like scrambled eggs. Diced peppers and tomatoes soften in olive oil until they collapse into a thick, jammy sauce, then beaten eggs are stirred in off the heat and left to barely set.
What you get is silky, saucy, and deeply savoury. It eats like a hug in a pan, best scooped up with crusty bread or Turkish flatbread alongside olives, white cheese, and black tea.
The one thing to watch: the eggs carry on cooking in the residual heat. Take the pan off the flame while they still look slightly underdone, and they will be perfect by the time they reach the table.

Warm the olive oil in the pan over a medium heat. Add the onion if using, and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Add the green and red peppers and cook for another 8 minutes, stirring often, until they are completely tender and starting to colour.

Add the tomatoes, chilli flakes, and salt. Stir well and cook over a medium heat for 10 minutes until the tomatoes have broken down into a thick sauce with very little liquid left. Taste and adjust the salt.

Pour the beaten eggs over the tomato sauce. Stir gently with the wooden spoon in slow, wide circles, drawing the set egg from the edges into the centre. After about 1 minute, when the egg is still slightly glossy but mostly set, take the pan off the heat. The residual heat will finish the cooking. Scatter parsley over the top and serve immediately from the pan.

rows.cause: Heat too high, or stirred too vigorously
rows.fix: Use medium-low heat for the egg stage. Stir gently and remove from heat while they look just underdone.

rows.cause: Tomatoes not cooked down enough before adding eggs
rows.fix: Cook the tomato sauce until almost all the liquid has evaporated before adding eggs.
Let the peppers soften fully before adding tomatoes; they should be very tender with no bite left.

content.text: Sucuklu menemen adds sliced Turkish sucuk sausage: fry it in the pan first until the fat runs, then remove it and build the sauce in the same fat, returning the sausage with the egg. For a simpler version with no onion, leave it out; the result is slightly sweeter and quicker.
Cook the pepper and tomato base up to 2 days ahead and refrigerate. Reheat gently in the pan, then add fresh beaten eggs to finish.

Menemen is a fixture of the Turkish kahvalti (breakfast table), appearing alongside white cheese, olives, cucumber, tomato, and tea. It is made in single portions at small lokantas or in large shared pans at home. The name comes from Menemen, a district of Izmir on the Aegean coast, though the dish is now eaten all over the country.
